title: Price Bands Read off the Vehicle Value Standing on a Listing
content:
The daily price a host may ask is fixed only once the vehicle value standing on the listing is the value the marketplace has settled on for it.

The band a listing is read against is settled from the vehicle value standing on the listing rather than from the class the vehicle sits in, and a price standing outside that band is brought inside it rather than refused.

| Vehicle value standing on the listing | Valuations in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date | Band | Ceiling a day | Floor a day |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 38000.01 USD or more | at least 1 | premium band | 320.00 USD | 75.00 USD |
| 18000.01 USD or more but below 38000.01 USD | at least 1 | standard band | 165.00 USD | 38.00 USD |
| any other case | — | entry band | as the entry band publishes | as the entry band publishes |

Every band above is a band of the Keyturn Vehicle Listing on which the price is asked.

As clauses: a listing whose vehicle value standing on it is 38000.01 USD or more and which carries at least one valuation in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date is read against the premium band, whose ceiling is 320.00 USD a day and whose floor is 75.00 USD a day; one whose standing vehicle value is 18000.01 USD or more but below 38000.01 USD and which carries at least one valuation in that window is read against the standard band, whose ceiling is 165.00 USD a day and whose floor is 38.00 USD a day; and any other listing is read against the entry band.

*Where the two conditions meet.* Both of the first two rows need a valuation in the window as well as the standing value: a listing standing at 52000.00 USD with no valuation in the rolling twelve months falls to the entry band, and the same listing with one valuation in that window is read against the premium band. A listing standing at exactly 38000.01 USD with a valuation in the window is on the premium row; at 38000.00 USD it is on the standard row.
